audit_findings.title: Merger completion would replace the valued claim and denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: 0.6539 AkzoNobel shares per Axalta share; Axalta shareholders are expected to own 45% of the combined company
audit_findings.mechanism: Completion replaces standalone Axalta OE, liabilities, bridge and share denominator with a claim on the combined company through the fixed exchange ratio.
audit_findings.evidence: Subject to the terms and conditions set forth in the Merger Agreement, at the Effective Time, each outstanding and issued ordinary share of the Company, par value $ 1.00 per share (other than any shares owned by the Company as treasury shares and any shares owned by AkzoNobel or any other direct or indirect wholly owned subsidiary of AkzoNobel), will be automatically converted into the right to receive 0.6539 (the “Exchange Ratio”) AkzoNobel ordinary shares, par value of € 0.50 per share.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated if the merger completes, but completion had not occurred at the valuation date. Until then, the AS_FILED standalone perimeter remains internally consistent. After closing, the present valuation would no longer describe the security owned, and the effect could increase or decrease value.
audit_findings.action: Confirm closing status and, immediately after completion, rebuild the valuation using combined-company OE, integration costs, all claims, the exchange ratio and the fully diluted combined share count.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized customer incentives may be omitted recurring reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: BIP carrying value increased $22m, from $169m to $191m, during 2025; 2025 amortization was $64m; the increase equals 7.2% of $306.4m anchor OE; exact net cash omission is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Accounting earnings deduct BIP amortization, but OE may need an additional deduction when cash spent to maintain customer commitments exceeds the amortization already recorded.
audit_findings.evidence: We do not receive a distinct service or good in return for these BIPs, but rather receive volume commitments and/or sole supplier status from our customers over the life of the contractual arrangements, which approximates a five-year weighted average useful life.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate recurring BIP investment and a $22m balance increase despite declining sales. They do not provide a complete reconciliation of cash disbursements, amortization, clawbacks, acquisitions and currency effects, so they do not establish the amount, if any, omitted from OE. The observed scale is large enough to require resolution.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile annual and first-half 2026 BIP cash disbursements to amortization, clawbacks, acquisitions and currency translation, classify maintenance versus growth spending, and rerun OE for any cash requirement not already represented by amortization.

audit_findings.title: Foreign cash may not be worth face value to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $544m of the $633m latest-quarter cash balance was held outside the US (86.0%); approximately $147m of withholding tax was unrecorded on permanently reinvested earnings; the distributable-cash haircut is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any tax, regulatory, operational or legal-entity restriction reduces the $633m cash addition in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, and 2024, we have not recorded a deferred tax liability related to withholding taxes of approximately $147 million and $95 million, respectively, on unremitted earnings of subsidiaries that are permanently invested.
audit_findings.explanation: The foreign concentration and potential withholding exposure are demonstrated, but the $147m relates to unremitted earnings rather than a proven tax charge against the reported cash. The record does not identify how much of the $633m is surplus, distributable or subject to leakage, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Map the June 2026 cash by entity and jurisdiction, identify minimum operating cash and distributable surplus, calculate actual withholding and local-tax leakage, and rerun the bridge with only net distributable cash.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded pensions may require cash beyond embedded expense
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 funded-status deficit $241m, equal to $1.11 per diluted share and 4.9% of base equity value; expected 2026 contributions $7m versus 2025 net periodic benefit cost of $19m
audit_findings.mechanism: Catch-up contributions or benefit payments exceeding the pension expense retained in OE would require an OE deduction or pension-related bridge adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: Many of these plans are underfunded or unfunded and the liabilities in relation to these plans will need to be satisfied as they mature from our operating reserves.
audit_findings.explanation: The $241m deficit is demonstrated, but it is not itself proof of an omitted equity claim because pension expense remains in OE. Near-term expected contributions of $7m are below the $19m expense embedded in 2025 earnings. The record does not establish whether later statutory funding will exceed the expense forecast, so the incremental valuation impact remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain plan-level statutory funding schedules and benefit-payment sources, compare annual cash funding with pension expense embedded in forecast OE, stress discount rates and asset returns, and rerun only for demonstrated excess funding.

audit_findings.title: Refinancing could raise the interest cost retained in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: required repayments of $521m in 2027 and $2,004m in 2029; 2025 interest expense $176m and first-half 2026 interest expense $75m; refinancing-rate impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE model, higher after-tax refinancing interest reduces forecast OE rather than being deducted separately through the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We may not be able to refinance any of our indebtedness on commercially reasonable terms or at all.
audit_findings.explanation: The maturities are demonstrated, but a higher refinancing rate is a future possibility rather than a current error. Axalta also reported $768m of revolver availability and had not yet selected refinancing terms. The effect must be monitored because the fixed-rate 2027 and 2029 notes and merger-related refinancing could reset interest expense.
audit_findings.action: When refinancing or merger financing terms become available, calculate the after-tax change from the interest cost embedded in OE and rerun the forecast without separately deducting ordinary principal.

audit_findings.title: Unrecorded customer guarantees create a contingent senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $25m unrecorded guarantees plus $14m secured by revolver letters of credit, or $39m total disclosed exposure; $0.18 per diluted share and 0.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Customer defaults would create cash payments not reflected in historical OE or the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025 and 2024, we had outstanding Customer Obligation Guarantees of $24 million and $23 million, respectively, excluding certain outstanding Customer Obligation Guarantees secured by letters of credit under the Revolving Credit Facility discussed further in Note 18.
audit_findings.explanation: No guarantee liability was recorded, so no expected loss is demonstrated. Even treating the entire $39m disclosed exposure as a loss would reduce base value by only about $0.18 per share, from $22.78 to approximately $22.60, and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $35.78 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that $14m captures all letter-of-credit-secured customer guarantees and review customer credit quality and loss history; rerun only if expected losses, rather than face exposure, become material.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: cited residual D&A of $60.5m to $70.3m, representing 19.0% to 21.8% of filed D&A in the listed years; 2025 anchor-year residual and eligible portion are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to OE and increase operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2016 $61.9m (19.2% of filed D&A); FY2017 $69.7m (20.1% of filed D&A); FY2018 $70.3m (19.0% of filed D&A); FY2019 $70.0m (19.8% of filed D&A); FY2020 $69.9m (21.8% of filed D&A); FY2022 $60.5m (20.0% of filed D&A); FY2024 $61.0m (21.8% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The conservative exclusion is demonstrated and cannot overstate value. However, the supplied residual amounts omit 2025, and no evidence classifies the residual components as eligible add-backs. The record therefore cannot establish the anchor-year OE increase or whether it is large enough to alter the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2025 D&A component reconciliation, classify each residual item against the OE add-back rules, and rerun the anchor and scenarios only for amounts supported as eligible non-economic D&A.
